deep.reconstruction:
Purpose: on 23 April (year not given on the page) Gauss determines the scale value of the main level ("Hauptlibelle") on a level tester. The page heading reads "Zur Bestimmung der Scale der Hauptlibelle". It follows the previous page (22 April), where the axis level ("Axenlibelle") was calibrated the same way and gave 1'' = 0.696 mm. The next page is the level journal of a circle instrument ("Kreis in Osten").

Data: The tester is set to a series of inclinations. The page heads the setting column '10' —' and writes the settings as 0 12'', 0 13'', 0 15'', 0 19.5'', 0 25'', 0 27'' (taken twice), 0 36.4'' and 0 42''. The "Spitzen nach innen" (points inward) heading presumably describes the mounting. For each setting the right and left bubble-end readings R and L (mm) are recorded:
- 12'': R 56.0, L off scale
- 13'': 55.8, 0
- 15'': 50.9, 3.9
- 19.5'': 40.1, 14.1
- 25'': 30.8, 24.6
- 27'': 27.4, 27.5
- 27'': 24.5, 30.8
- 36.4'': 11.1, 42.1
- 42'': 1.1, 54.0

Reduction (rule inferred by me, verified line by line): with the adopted scale value 1'' = 1.8 mm, each setting t is reduced to the inclination at which the bubble would be symmetric (both ends at about 27.4 mm, the note under the heading):
  T = t + ((R − L)/2)/1.8.
For the first line only R is available, so Gauss uses T = t + (R − 27.4)/1.8. This explains the isolated '27 mm 4'.

Checks of each line:
- 12 + 28.6/1.8 = 27.89 → 27.9
- 13 + 27.9/1.8 = 28.50 → 28.5
- 15 + 23.5/1.8 = 28.06 → 28.1
- 19.5 + 13.0/1.8 = 26.72 → 26.7
- 25 + 3.1/1.8 = 26.72 → 26.7
- 27 − 0.05/1.8 = 26.97 → 27.0
- 27 − 3.15/1.8 = 25.25 → 25.3
- 36.4 − 15.5/1.8 = 27.79 → 27.8
- 42 − 26.45/1.8 = 27.31 → 27.3

The reduced values scatter (25.3–28.5) with no systematic trend. Gauss evidently takes this as confirming 1'' ≈ 1.8 mm, i.e. 1 mm ≈ 0.56''.

My check by least squares on the bubble-centre displacement (R − L)/2 against t over the eight two-ended lines gives a slope of about −1.84 mm per second. This agrees with the adopted 1.8 within the scatter. The mean half-sum (R + L)/2 of the bubble is ≈ 27.4 mm, the reference point. The bubble length is about 47–57 mm, varying slightly, presumably with temperature or reading.
errors: No arithmetic errors: every reduced value agrees with T = t + (R−L)/(2·1.8) to the 0.1'' written.

The adopted 1.8 mm/'' is a rounded value; a least-squares slope over all lines gives ≈1.84 mm/''. The difference lies within the scatter of the readings (repeat at 27'' differs by 1.7''), so it is not an error.

results.what: Calibration of a spirit-level scale value on a level tester (inclination steps vs. bubble-end readings, reduction of each observation to a common bubble position with an assumed scale value, checking constancy)
results.modern_name: Level (bubble) sensitivity / scale-value calibration with a level trier (Libellenprüfer)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard instrumental practice of 18th–19th c. astronomers/geodesists (Reichenbach-era instrument makers, Bessel, Gauss, etc.)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine observational/instrumental calibration data. Gauss's work with levels and meridian-circle instruments at Göttingen is well known. Nothing mathematically non-standard is on the page.

checkable.asserts: First line (right end only) reduces to 27.9''.
Reduction rule T = t + ((R-L)/2)/1.8 reproduces all written reduced values.
Least-squares slope of bubble-centre displacement vs inclination is about -1.84 mm per arcsecond, consistent with adopted 1''=1.8 mm.

transcription_corrections: The third column on line '0 13' reads '0' (left end reading 0 mm), not a separator; the first line's left reading is blank/'....' (off scale).
Header likely reads 'Spitzen nach innen' over the setting column and 'Rechts' / 'Links' (right/left bubble end) over the two reading columns; '10' —' appears as a heading over the settings column.
'27mm4' under the heading is the reference bubble position (mean of the two ends) to which the observations are reduced.
